mainTopic: שמואל's rule about כרמלית, רב's low house and אביי's pit, the dispute over חורי רשות הרבים, and רב חסדא's stick in a רשות היחיד
overview: The גמרא first works out what שמואל meant by 'no domain above ten טפחים.' It cannot mean רשות הרבים, because that is already an explicit משנה. So it means כרמלית, which חז"ל gave one leniency from each side: it needs 4×4 like רשות היחיד, and it stops at ten like רשות הרבים. Next, with גופא, the גמרא returns to רב's ruling about a low house: one may carry anywhere on its roof, but only four אמות inside. אביי adds that digging a 4×4 pit that reaches ten makes the whole house private, because חורי רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד. אביי and רבא then argue whether חורי רשות הרבים are like רשות הרבים. אביי defends his view against challenges from a corner next to רשות הרבים and from רבי יוחנן's sticky fig cake, and the גמרא proves that the משנה's wall has no hole. Finally, the גמרא turns to רב חסדא's ruling that a stick in a רשות היחיד counts at any height. It asks whether he follows רבי, who does not require a 4×4 resting place, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Suggesting שמואל meant the public domain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries a new reading of שמואל: he meant that רשות הרבים does not extend above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, perhaps שמואל meant that there is no רשות הרבים above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: An earlier reading of שמואל's words did not work, so the גמרא now offers a new one. It suggests he was talking about רשות הרבים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means 'rather': an earlier reading was dropped and a new one is proposed. On this reading, שמואל taught that the public domain only counts up to ten טפחים from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals replacing a rejected idea with a new one
Above ten טפחים (handbreadths) from the ground

phrases.english: Rather, that there is no public domain
above ten handbreadths

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּאֵין רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier rejected reading of שמואל's statement (on the previous amud)
steps.terutzMaskana: Proposed (and rejected in step 2): שמואל's 'no domain above ten' refers to רשות הרבים

steps.title: That would just repeat a משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: if that is all שמואל meant, he would just be repeating an explicit משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion from step 1. An אמורא would not bother to state something a משנה already says clearly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a redundancy challenge. The new reading is not wrong in content; it is just pointless as a new teaching. The proof comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is a משנה!' The statement is already found in the משנה, so it is redundant

phrases.english: It is a mishna!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading proposed in step 1
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading שמואל as speaking about רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An אמורא does not restate a law that is already explicit in a משנה

steps.title: The משנה about throwing at a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה showing that רשות הרבים ends at ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: one who throws an object four אמות in the public domain and it lands on a wall above ten טפחים is like one who throws into the air. Below ten טפחים, it is like throwing onto the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up its objection by quoting the משנה. The משנה already teaches that the public domain stops at ten טפחים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the object sticks to the wall above ten, it is treated as if it never landed in רשות הרבים, so there is no liability for carrying four אמות. Below ten, it counts as landing in רשות הרבים. This is exactly the reading suggested for שמואל, so that reading would be redundant.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the distance that makes carrying in רשות הרבים liable
Like throwing into the air, as if the object never landed

phrases.english: As we learned: One who throws four cubits
onto a wall, above ten handbreadths
is like one who throws into the air.
Below ten handbreadths
is like one who throws onto the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַזּוֹרֵק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בַּכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the objection of step 2
steps.raayaObject: The claim that 'no רשות הרבים above ten' is already a משנה

steps.title: שמואל meant כרמלית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that שמואל meant that כרמלית does not extend above ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he meant כרמלית: there is no כרמלית above ten טפחים.
steps.whatsHappening: After rejecting the other readings, the גמרא settles on this one: שמואל was teaching about כרמלית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reading is not stated in any משנה, so it is a real new teaching. It means a spot more than ten טפחים above a כרמלית is not part of the כרמלית.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic in-between domain, neither fully private nor fully public (e.g., a field or sea)

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'no domain above ten טפחים' means: no כרמלית above ten.

phrases.english: Rather, a karmelit,
that there is no karmelit above ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כַּרְמְלִית, דְּאֵין כַּרְמְלִית לְמַעְלָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading of steps 1-3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no כרמלית above ten טפחים

steps.title: חז"ל gave כרמלית leniencies from both domains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that חז"ל applied to כרמלית some leniencies of רשות היחיד and some of רשות הרבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן were lenient with כרמלית, giving it leniencies of רשות היחיד and leniencies of רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a general principle about כרמלית. The next two steps spell out each leniency.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since כרמלית is only a rabbinic domain, חז"ל picked the easier rule from each side. This explains why כרמלית ends at ten, which is a feature borrowed from רשות הרבים.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן were lenient with it

phrases.english: And the Sages were lenient with it
with leniencies of the private domain
and with leniencies of the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַקִּילוּ בַּהּ רַבָּנַן מִקּוּלֵּי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד וּמִקּוּלֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the conclusion of step 4
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כרמלית takes the leniencies of both רשות היחיד and רשות הרבים

steps.title: The private-domain leniency: needs four handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: Like רשות היחיד, a כרמלית must be at least 4×4 טפחים; otherwise it is only a מקום פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leniency of רשות היחיד: only if there is an area of four טפחים is it a כרמלית. If not, it is just a מקום פטור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first leniency, which is borrowed from רשות היחיד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשות היחיד needs a minimum area of 4×4 טפחים, while רשות הרבים has no such minimum. כרמלית borrows the minimum, which is the lenient side, so a small spot under 4×4 is an exempt area where carrying in or out is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An area of four by four טפחים
An exempt area, which is not a domain at all

phrases.english: Leniencies of the private domain:
that if there is an area of four
then it is a karmelit,
and if not,
it is merely an exempt area.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקּוּלֵּי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד — דְּאִי אִיכָּא מָקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the first half of step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרמלית needs at least 4×4 טפחים; below that it is a מקום פטור

steps.title: The public-domain leniency: only up to ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: Like רשות הרבים, a כרמלית extends only up to ten טפחים, not above.
steps.simpleTranslation: The leniency of רשות הרבים: up to ten טפחים it is a כרמלית; above ten טפחים it is not a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second leniency, which is borrowed from רשות הרבים. This is the source of שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A רשות היחיד goes all the way up to the sky, while רשות הרבים stops at ten. כרמלית borrows the lenient side and stops at ten, so the space above it is a מקום פטור.
steps.whatToRemember: כרמלית takes the easier rule from each side: it needs 4×4 like רשות היחיד, and it stops at ten טפחים like רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: Leniencies of the public domain:
that up to ten handbreadths
it is a karmelit;
above ten handbreadths
it is not a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקּוּלֵּי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים — דְּעַד עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים הוּא דְּהָוְיָא כַּרְמְלִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Details the second half of step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כרמלית does not extend above ten טפחים

steps.title: רב: a low house whose roof reaches ten
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב's ruling: if a house is under ten inside but reaches ten with its roof, one may carry anywhere on the roof, but only four אמות inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the statement itself: רב גידל said in the name of רב חייא בר יוסף in the name of רב: a house whose inside is not ten טפחים high, but whose roof brings it to ten. On its roof, one may carry on all of it. Inside it, one may carry only four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The word גופא tells us the גמרא is going back to discuss a statement it quoted earlier. It now examines רב's ruling directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From outside, the walls plus the roof reach ten טפחים, so the roof is a raised area of ten and counts as a full רשות היחיד. Inside, the space is less than ten high, so it is only a כרמלית, and one may carry only within four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself': returning to analyze a statement quoted earlier

steps.confusionAlert: The same house has two different statuses: the roof is a רשות היחיד, but the inside is a כרמלית. The difference is that the height is measured from the outside for the roof and from the inside for the interior.

phrases.english: To the matter itself:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Giddel said that Rav Ḥiyya bar Yosef said that Rav said:
A house whose inside is not ten
and its roofing completes it to ten:
on its roof, one may carry on all of it;
inside it, one may not carry in it
except within four cubits.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל discussion and returns to רב's statement quoted earlier on the דף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Roof: a full רשות היחיד. Inside: a כרמלית (four אמות only).

steps.title: אביי: digging a pit makes the whole house private
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that if one digs a 4×4 pit in the floor so that the height there reaches ten, one may carry in the entire house.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: and if he dug out four by four טפחים in it and brought it to ten, one may carry in the whole house.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a new case to רב's ruling. A small dug-out area can change the status of the whole house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pit, measured from its bottom to the ceiling, is ten high and 4×4 wide, so it is a real רשות היחיד. Surprisingly, אביי says the rest of the house, which is still under ten, now becomes permitted too. The reason comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: In all of it (the whole house)

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם חָקַק בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
phrases.english: And if he dug out in it four by four
and brought it to ten,
it is permitted to carry in all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: וְאִם חָקַק בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to the 'inside' half of רב's ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A 4×4 pit reaching ten makes the whole house a רשות היחיד

steps.title: Why does the whole house become private?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind אביי's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the rest of the house, which is under ten, would become permitted. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the pit itself meets the requirements of a רשות היחיד. The question is how the remaining low area gets that status.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the low part of the house becomes a רשות היחיד

steps.title: The rest of the house is like holes of the private domain
steps.stepSummary: The low area around the pit counts as חורי רשות היחיד, and holes of a רשות היחיד are treated like the רשות היחיד itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is considered the holes of רשות היחיד, and the holes of רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The rest of the house is treated as a side area attached to the private pit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the pit is a רשות היחיד, the low area around it is seen as an attachment, like holes in its walls. Such attachments take on the status of the main domain even though they lack its measurements.

keyTerms.meaning: Holes (side recesses) of the private domain
Are considered like, are similar to

phrases.english: It is the holes of the private domain,
and the holes of the private domain
are considered like the private domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָוֵי חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The low area counts as חורי רשות היחיד, which share the status of רשות היחיד

steps.title: Source: the holes of a private domain are private
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites an accepted teaching that חורי רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: the holes of רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the answer of step 11 by quoting an established rule that everyone accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is quoted with no dissent, so it is agreed upon by all. This makes it a solid basis for אביי's ruling.

phrases.english: As it was stated:

phrases.aramaic: חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד כִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד דָּמוּ,
phrases.english: The holes of the private domain are considered like the private domain;

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִיתְּמַר: חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד כִּרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the rule used in step 11
steps.raayaObject: The rule that חורי רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד
steps.raayaSupportSource: A statement of the אמוראים (איתמר) accepted by all

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue about holes of the public domain
steps.stepSummary: אביי holds that חורי רשות הרבים are like רשות הרבים; רבא holds they are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding the holes of רשות הרבים: אביי says they are like רשות הרבים. רבא says they are not like רשות הרבים.
steps.whatsHappening: The quoted teaching continues with a מחלוקת. Everyone agrees about private-domain holes, but אביי and רבא disagree about public-domain holes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי applies the same logic to both domains: a hole takes the status of its main domain. רבא disagrees for רשות הרבים. For him, such a hole is a כרמלית or a מקום פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: Holes (recesses) in the walls of the public domain

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that holes of רשות היחיד are like רשות היחיד; this is why a 4×4 pit makes a whole low house private. For holes of רשות הרבים, אביי says they are like רשות הרבים and רבא says they are not.

phrases.english: The holes of the public domain:
Abaye says they are considered like the public domain.
Rava says:
They are not considered like the public domain.

steps.triggerLanguage: חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים, אַבָּיֵי אוֹמֵר כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted teaching from step 12 with a disputed case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: חורי רשות הרבים are like רשות הרבים. רבא: they are not.

steps.title: רבא challenges אביי from a corner next to the public domain
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks אביי: if holes of רשות הרבים count as רשות הרבים, why does a corner next to רשות הרבים count only as a כרמלית, as רבי יוחנן said?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: You say that holes of the public domain are treated like the public domain. Then how is that different from what רב דימי reported in the name of רבי יוחנן? רבי יוחנן said the כרמלית rule was needed only for a corner next to the public domain. That corner should be like the holes of the public domain!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks אביי's position from Step 13. He brings a ruling of רבי יוחנן that seems to contradict it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said a corner next to רשות הרבים is a כרמלית. It is not full רשות הרבים. But a corner is a lot like a hole: it is a small side area attached to the public domain. So if holes count as רשות הרבים, the corner should count too.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

phrases.english: Rava said to Abaye:
According to you, who said

phrases.aramaic: חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ,
phrases.english: holes of the public domain are like the public domain,
how is it different from this
that when Rav Dimi came
he said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
it was needed only
for a corner adjacent to the public domain,
phrases.notes: It teaches that such a corner is a כרמלית.

phrases.english: but let it be like the holes of the public domain?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's position from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that חורי רשות הרבים are like רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A corner next to רשות הרבים is like a hole. Yet רבי יוחנן rules it is only a כרמלית.

steps.title: A corner is hard to use, but holes are easy to use
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that a corner is inconvenient to use, while holes are convenient to use, so holes join the public domain.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the corner is not convenient to use. Here, the holes are convenient to use.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself. He shows that the corner and the hole are not the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What counts is whether people actually use the space easily. The public uses holes easily, so holes become part of רשות הרבים. A corner is awkward to use, so it stays a כרמלית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key test: how easily the public uses a space decides its status.

phrases.english: There, its use is not convenient;
phrases.notes: "Its use" here means using the corner.

phrases.english: here, its use is convenient.
phrases.notes: "Its use" here means using the holes.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם לָא נִיחָא תַּשְׁמִישְׁתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the two cases (convenience of use)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A corner and a hole are the same kind of side space.
steps.terutzMaskana: Holes are easy to use, so they join רשות הרבים. Corners are not easy to use, so they do not.

steps.title: A משנה about throwing onto a wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. If someone throws four אמות onto a wall in רשות הרבים, above ten טפחים it is like throwing into the air. Below ten it is like throwing onto the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה: If someone throws an object four cubits onto a wall, above ten handbreadths it is like throwing into the air. Below ten handbreadths it is like throwing onto the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second challenge to אביי. It begins by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Above ten טפחים the object is not in רשות הרבים, so there is no liability. Below ten it counts as resting in רשות הרבים, so the thrower is liable for moving it four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, the distance that makes one liable in רשות הרבים
Like throwing into the air (no liability)

phrases.english: We learned: One who throws four cubits onto a wall,
above ten — it is like throwing into the air.
below ten handbreadths — it is like throwing onto the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַזּוֹרֵק אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת בַּכּוֹתֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to אביי, based on a משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A throw onto a wall below ten טפחים counts as landing on the ground. Above ten it counts as landing in the air.

steps.title: But the object never rested on the wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls an earlier question: why is it like throwing onto the ground if the object did not rest on the wall?
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed it: What does 'like throwing onto the ground' mean? It did not rest there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא recalls a known question about this משנה. Liability needs the object to come to rest, and a thrown object usually bounces off a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You are liable for carrying on שבת only when the object comes to rest. A thrown object usually bounces off a wall and does not stay there. So how can the משנה call it landing on the ground?

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
What does 'like throwing onto the ground' mean?
But it did not rest!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָוֵינַן בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case of the משנה quoted in Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the object counts as resting if it hit the wall and did not stay.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the case is a sticky fig cake
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the משנה is about a juicy fig cake, which sticks to the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: They taught it about a juicy fig cake.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. The משנה is about an object that sticks to the wall and stays there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A juicy fig cake sticks to the wall, so it truly comes to rest there. Since the spot is below ten טפחים in רשות הרבים, the thrower is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: A juicy (fat) fig cake that sticks

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said,
they taught it about a juicy fig cake.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, בִּדְבֵילָה שְׁמֵינָה שָׁנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The object is a sticky fig cake that stays on the wall.

steps.title: Why not a stone that landed in a hole?
steps.stepSummary: If holes of רשות הרבים count as רשות הרבים, רבי יוחנן could have explained the משנה as an ordinary stone landing in a hole below ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think holes of the public domain are like the public domain, why do I need to explain it as a juicy fig cake? Let us explain it as a stone or object that came to rest in a hole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses רבי יוחנן's explanation to challenge אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to אביי, a hole in the wall below ten טפחים is part of רשות הרבים. So a plain stone landing in that hole would make the thrower liable. Since רבי יוחנן chose an unusual case instead, it seems he does not hold like אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you were to think)
To set up (explain) the case as

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that

phrases.aramaic: חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ,
phrases.english: holes of the public domain are like the public domain,
why do I need to explain it as a juicy fig cake?
Let us explain it as a stone or object,
that came to rest in a hole!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ חוֹרֵי רְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים כִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים דָּמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי יוחנן's answer in Step 18 to attack אביי's view from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's rule that חורי רשות הרבים are like רשות הרבים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If holes count as רשות הרבים, a simpler case was available: a stone resting in a hole. רבי יוחנן's unusual case suggests holes do not count.

steps.title: First answer: a stone bounces back
steps.stepSummary: אביי sometimes answered that a stone or object bounces back out and does not settle in the hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he would answer: A stone or object is different, because it bounces back.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives his first answer to the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hard object thrown at a wall usually bounces out instead of settling in a hole. So landing in a hole is not the normal case. A sticky fig cake that stays put is the more natural way to explain the משנה.

phrases.english: Sometimes he would answer it:
a stone or object is different,
because it bounces back.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין מְשַׁנֵּי לַהּ, שָׁאנֵי צְרוֹר וְחֵפֶץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical distinction: hard objects do not stay in holes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A stone could easily be the case, landing in a hole.
steps.terutzMaskana: A stone bounces out, so the fig cake case is the better explanation.

steps.title: Second answer: the wall has no hole
steps.stepSummary: אביי sometimes answered that the משנה is speaking about a wall with no hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes he would answer: It is about a wall that has no hole.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second, different answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wall in the משנה has no hole, a stone has nowhere to rest. Only a sticky object can stay on it. So the fig cake case says nothing against אביי's view of holes.

keyTerms.meaning: That does not have in it

phrases.english: Sometimes he would answer it:
it is about a wall that has no hole.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין מְשַׁנֵּי לַהּ, בְּכוֹתֶל דְּלֵית בֵּיהּ חוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, independent answer to Step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wall in the משנה might have holes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wall has no hole, so only a sticky object can rest on it.

steps.title: Proof from the first half of the משנה that the wall has no hole
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the משנה says that above ten it is like throwing into the air. If the wall had a hole, the object would have rested in a private-domain hole and he would be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this? From what the first half teaches: If he threw above ten handbreadths, it is like throwing into the air. If you think the wall has a hole, why is it like throwing into the air? It rested in a hole!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves אביי's second answer from the first part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A hole above ten טפחים in a wall counts as a רשות היחיד. If the wall had such a hole, an object resting there would make the thrower liable for moving it from רשות הרבים into רשות היחיד. Since the משנה says he is not liable (like throwing into the air), the wall must have no hole.

keyTerms.meaning: From what the first clause teaches

steps.whatToRemember: אביי defends his view that holes of רשות הרבים count as רשות הרבים in three ways. A corner is hard to use, unlike a hole. A stone bounces out of a hole. And the משנה's wall has no hole, which the first half of the משנה supports. Steps 23-25 finish this proof.
steps.confusionAlert: Above ten טפחים, a hole would be a רשות היחיד, not part of רשות הרבים. That is why a hole there would create liability for throwing into a private domain.

phrases.english: From where do we know?
From what the first clause teaches:
if he threw above ten handbreadths —
it is like throwing into the air.
And if it enters your mind
that it is a wall with a hole in it,
why is it like throwing into the air?
It rested in a hole!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? מִדְּקָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the second answer of Step 21.
steps.raayaObject: That the wall in the משנה has no hole
steps.raayaSupportSource: The first clause of the משנה: above ten טפחים it is like throwing into the air

steps.title: What if the holes are simply too small?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a possible objection to אביי's proof. Maybe the משנה's wall does have holes, but they are smaller than ארבעה על ארבעה, so they do not count as a real place.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that the משנה is talking about holes that are not four by four טפחים...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines someone trying to escape אביי's proof. It is setting up the next move, where this escape will be blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's proof says that if the wall had a hole, the object would rest inside it and the thrower would be חייב. Someone could answer that the holes are too small to matter, since a place usually needs ארבעה על ארבעה to count as a resting spot. If that were true, the משנה could still be talking about a wall with holes.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (introduces a possible objection)
Four by four טפחים, the usual minimum size for a place to count
That do not have in them

phrases.english: And if you will say that the Mishnah
phrases.notes: Opens a possible escape from אביי's proof

phrases.english: is about holes that do not have four by four
phrases.notes: So the holes would be too small to count as a place

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא מַתְנִיתִין דְּלֵית בְּהוּ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a possible objection to the proof in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's proof that the משנה is about a wall with no hole
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wall might have holes that are too small (less than ארבעה על ארבעה) to count as a resting place. Then the משנה could still be talking about a wall with holes.

steps.title: Even a tiny hole is a subject of dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the objection using רבי חייא's teaching. An object landing in a hole of any size above ten is subject to the מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and רבנן about חוקקין להשלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב יהודה said in the name of רבי חייא: If someone threw an object above ten טפחים and it went and landed in a hole of any size, we have reached the dispute of רבי מאיר and רבנן. רבי מאיר holds that we imagine carving out the space to complete the size, and רבנן hold that we do not imagine carving it out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that small holes do not matter. It quotes רבי חייא, who says that even a tiny hole leads straight into a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a small hole is treated as if it were carved out to full size, so it counts as a real place in the רשות היחיד. If the משנה were about small holes, at least רבי מאיר would make the thrower חייב. The משנה, however, gives a simple rule with no dispute, so the small-hole explanation does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: We imagine carving out the space to complete the required size
We do not imagine carving it out; the space is judged by its actual size

steps.confusionAlert: חוקקין להשלים does not mean anyone actually carves the hole. It is a legal way of looking at the hole: if it could be widened, רבי מאיר treats it as if it already were.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say that Rabbi Chiya said:
phrases.notes: This quote is brought to knock down that suggestion.

phrases.english: If someone threw above ten handbreadths
and it went and came to rest in a hole of any size,
phrases.notes: Even a hole smaller than four by four

phrases.english: we have arrived at the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis.
For Rabbi Meir holds: we carve out to complete.
phrases.notes: The small hole is treated as full size, so the thrower is חייב

phrases.english: And the Rabbis hold: we do not carve out to complete.
phrases.notes: The small hole stays small and does not count

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the escape suggested in Step 23
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the משנה is about holes smaller than ארבעה על ארבעה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A small hole is still disputed: רבי מאיר treats it as full size. So the משנה's simple, undisputed rule cannot be about a wall with small holes.

steps.title: So the משנה means a wall with no hole
steps.stepSummary: With the escape blocked, the גמרא concludes that the משנה is about a wall with no hole at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it proven from this that the משנה is about a wall with no hole in it? Yes, it is proven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's proof and accepts it. The משנה is talking about a smooth wall with no hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No hole means there is nowhere for the object to rest, so it is just like throwing into the air, as the משנה says. This also supports אביי's second answer in Step 21: רבי יוחנן could not explain the משנה as a stone landing in a hole below ten, because the משנה is about a wall without holes.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it so that... (leads to a conclusion)
Learn from it; it is proven

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's wall above ten is "like throwing into the air" because it has no hole. A hole, even a tiny one according to רבי מאיר, would be a resting place in the רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not proven from this
that it is about a wall that has no hole in it?
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion after the objection was rejected in Step 24
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה about throwing onto a wall above ten is talking about a wall with no hole, which supports אביי.

steps.title: רב חסדא: a stick in a private domain counts at any height
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב חסדא's statement mentioned earlier. If someone throws an object and it lands on top of a stick standing in a רשות היחיד, he is חייב even if the stick is a hundred אמות tall.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the statement itself. רב חסדא said: If someone stuck a stick into the ground in a רשות היחיד, and he threw an object and it landed on top of the stick, he is חייב even if the stick is a hundred אמות high, because the רשות היחיד rises up to the sky.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion by going back to a statement it quoted earlier in passing. It now studies רב חסדא's ruling directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a רשות היחיד extends all the way up, the top of the stick is still inside the private domain no matter how tall the stick is. Throwing from the רשות הרבים onto it is a full transfer into the רשות היחיד, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself; the גמרא now returns to a statement it mentioned before
He stuck a stick into the ground
The private domain rises up to the sky

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next question. The top of a stick is very small, much less than ארבעה על ארבעה, so the גמרא will ask whether רב חסדא's ruling depends on a minority opinion.

phrases.english: The matter itself. Rav Chisda said:
phrases.notes: Returns to a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: If one stuck a stick in the private domain,
and threw, and it came to rest on top of it,
even if it is a hundred cubits high, he is liable,

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁרְשׁוּת הַיָּחִיד עוֹלָה עַד לָרָקִיעַ.
phrases.english: because the private domain rises up to the sky.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion by returning to רב חסדא's statement mentioned earlier
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An object thrown onto a stick standing in a רשות היחיד makes the thrower חייב at any height, because the רשות היחיד goes up to the sky.

steps.title: Does רב חסדא follow רבי's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב חסדא's ruling follows only רבי. In a ברייתא, רבי makes a person חייב when an object lands on a ledge of any size, while the חכמים exempt him. That means רבי does not require a resting place of ארבעה על ארבעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that רב חסדא ruled like רבי? For it was taught in a ברייתא: If someone threw an object and it landed on a ledge of any size, רבי makes him חייב and the חכמים exempt him. This shows that, according to רבי, we do not need a place of four by four.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רב חסדא's ruling depends on רבי's side of a dispute in a ברייתא. This would mean the ruling does not fit the majority view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The top of a stick is tiny, so רב חסדא seems to hold that a small spot counts as a resting place. In the ברייתא, only רבי says a small ledge counts, while the חכמים require ארבעה על ארבעה. So רב חסדא would appear to agree with רבי against the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (suggests that an אמורא depends on one side of an earlier dispute)
A ledge or projection sticking out from a wall

phrases.english: Shall we say that Rav Chisda spoke in accordance with Rebbi?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: זָרַק וְנָח עַל גַּבֵּי זִיז כׇּל שֶׁהוּא —
phrases.english: As it was taught: If he threw and it came to rest on a ledge of any size,
Rebbi holds him liable and the Sages exempt him.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לָא בָּעֵינַן מָקוֹם אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה.
phrases.english: This shows that, according to Rebbi, we do not need a place of four by four.
phrases.notes: Just like the small top of רב חסדא's stick

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַב חִסְדָּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's ruling from Step 26 by linking it to רבי's minority opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's ruling about the stick in the רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The top of a stick is smaller than ארבעה על ארבעה. Only רבי says that a resting place of any size counts, while the חכמים disagree. So רב חסדא seems to follow a minority view.
